newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. Security Council extends Iraqi oil-for-food deal.
newsitem.headline: U.N. Security Council extends Iraqi oil-for-food deal.

text.p: The U.N. Security Council voted unanimously on Wednesday to approve a six-month renewal of its "oil-for-food" deal with Iraq.

Under the deal, which went into force on Dec. 10 and expires on June 7, Iraq has been allowed to sell $2 billion worth of oil to buy food, medicine and other necessities to help alleviate the effects of sanctions in force since its August 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
The new council resolution, adopted in a two-minute meeting without speeches, would renew the arrangement for another 180-day period beginning at 12:01 a.m. EDT (0401 GMT) on June 8.

On the basis of reports from Secretary-General Kofi Annan and the U.N. sanctions committee, the 15-member council said it would conduct a "thorough review of all aspects" of the scheme after 90 days and again before the end of the 180-day period.

The resolution says the council "expresses its intention, prior to the end of the 180-day period, to consider favourably renewal of the provisions of this resolution, provided that the reports...indicate that those provisions are being satisfactorily implemented."

A major preoccupation of the council has been to ensure that all sectors of the Iraqi population benefit from the supplies bought with the limited oil sales, not just those groups favoured by the Baghdad government. U.N. observers have been deployed in the country to ensure this.
